# Kyoto Family Trip Plan: 4 Days in Early April

A relaxed, blossom-focused plan for 2 adults and 1 child with **easy transit**, **one kid-friendly museum**, and **no more than 2 hotel changes**. I’m assuming you want a **single-base stay in central Kyoto** to keep transfers simple and the pace comfortable.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival, Central Kyoto, and Light Blossom Walks
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive in Kyoto and check in near **Kyoto Station** or **Karasuma** for the easiest train/subway access.
- **Afternoon:** Keep it light with **Kyoto Station area**, **Kyoto Tower viewpoint**, and a slow stroll through **Shosei-en Garden** if energy is good.
- **Food:** Simple first-night dinner near the station: udon, curry rice, or a family-friendly set meal.
- **Evening:** Early night to reset for blossom sightseeing.

### Day 2: Philosopher’s Path, Nanzen-ji, and Higashiyama
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Head early to **Philosopher’s Path** for cherry blossoms before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Walk or short-taxi to **Nanzen-ji** and nearby temple grounds; keep the route flexible so the child can rest.
- **Food:** Lunch in **Okazaki / Higashiyama** with a casual noodle or tofu set.
- **Evening:** Return to the hotel for downtime; optional short stop at **Gion** if everyone still has energy.

### Day 3: Kid-Friendly Museum Day + Maruyama Park
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Morning:** Visit the **Kyoto City Zoo area** or **Kyoto Municipal Museum of School History** only if you want a very light add-on; otherwise keep the main focus on the museum below.
- **Midday:** Spend your main indoor block at the **Kyoto Railway Museum** — this is the best kid-friendly museum choice for your trip.
- **Afternoon:** Go to **Umekoji Park** for open space, then continue to **Maruyama Park** for blossoms and a relaxed family break.
- **Food:** Family lunch near the museum; dinner back near Kyoto Station for convenience.

### Day 4: Arashiyama and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Morning:** Start early for **Arashiyama** to enjoy the bamboo grove and riverside before it gets busy.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one easy add-on: **Tenryu-ji gardens** or a short river walk, then head back and pack calmly.
- **Food:** Lunch in Arashiyama, then a simple early dinner or station bento if you’re departing later.
- **Evening:** Leave at least 2–3 hours of buffer before any onward train.

## Best-Use Budget Plan for ¥180,000

### Spending Mix
- **Hotel:** ¥80,000–¥110,000 for 3–4 nights in a family room or 2-room setup
- **Local transport:** ¥8,000–¥15,000
- **Admission / activities:** ¥8,000–¥18,000
- **Food:** ¥35,000–¥50,000
- **Snacks / extras / buffer:** ¥10,000–¥20,000

### Practical Fit
| Category | Plan | Why it works |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel changes | **1 hotel base** | Simplest for a child and best for transit efficiency |
| Transport style | **Train + subway + occasional taxi** | Fast, easy, and low-stress for short hops |
| Blossom strategy | **Early mornings** | Better photos, fewer crowds, more comfortable pace |
| Indoor backup | **Kyoto Railway Museum** | Strong family-friendly option if weather changes |

## Quick Actions
